question: A team is deciding which steps of its onboarding process to hand to Claude and which to keep. Which two steps should stay with a person? Select two.
options: A) The final decision on whether a new hire has passed the probation review for this quarter.
B) The conversation with a new joiner about a personal difficulty raised in their first week.
C) Drafting the standard welcome message that each of the new joiners receives on their first day.
D) Turning the existing onboarding handbook into a shorter checklist for the new joiners.
E) Summarising last year's onboarding survey feedback into a set of recurring themes.
correct_answers: A) The final decision on whether a new hire has passed the probation review for this quarter.
B) The conversation with a new joiner about a personal difficulty raised in their first week.
explanations: Correct. A probation outcome affects someone's employment, so the decision needs the accountability only a person can carry.
Correct. A personal difficulty raised by a colleague calls for human judgment and duty of care, not a delegated reply.
Incorrect. A standard welcome message is a low-stakes, repetitive draft, which is a good candidate for delegation.
Incorrect. Condensing an existing handbook is well-specified text work that a person can review before it is published.
Incorrect. Theming survey feedback is high-volume analysis whose output the team can check against the underlying responses.
